What can I build with this?

You can build AI-powered automation workflows, smart data processing pipelines, content generation tools, and intelligent task routing systems. Aeye is designed for any product that needs to process inputs, apply reasoning, and deliver structured outputs — from internal tools to customer-facing features.
Do I need AI or machine learning experience?

No. Aeye abstracts the underlying AI complexity through clean APIs and workflow primitives. You define what you need — inputs, tasks, and expected outputs — and Aeye handles the rest. Basic programming knowledge is enough to get started.

Install the SDK via npm, pip, or CLI — setup takes under five minutes. Authenticate with your API key, define your workflow, and start sending requests. Aeye returns structured outputs you can plug directly into your existing application logic.
Can it work with my current tools?

Yes. Aeye is built to fit into existing stacks without replacing them. It integrates with common data sources, APIs, and platforms. If your tool can send an HTTP request or run a script, it can connect to Aeye.
Is it suitable for production use?

Yes. Aeye is designed with reliability and consistency in mind — the same input produces the same quality output every time. Teams already use it in live products and automated pipelines, with monitoring and priority support available on higher plans.

Designing AI Workflows That Actually Work
Every good workflow starts with understanding. Our tool was designed around a simple principle: developers move fastest when visibility, action, and feedback are all in one loop.
Three modules. One continuous cycle. Each phase supports the next — keeping you focused on building, not context-switching.
Step 1: Inspect — See what’s really happening
The Inspect module is your visibility layer. It lets you explore structured data, logs, and payloads in real time — the same way you’d read a console, but with clarity and context.
View and filter request payloads or event logs.
View and filter request payloads or event logs.
Pin important signals for quick reference.
Pin important signals for quick reference.
Search structured data without leaving your workspace.
Search structured data without leaving your workspace.
It’s the foundation for everything else, because before you automate or monitor, you need to understand what’s going on.
Step 2: Automate — Turn repetitive work into repeatable flow
Once you can see your data clearly, the next step is Automate. This module lets you turn any manual debugging step, build routine, or test trigger into a defined workflow.
Run a cleanup task when a new build completes.
Run a cleanup task when a new build completes.
Trigger notifications when an endpoint changes state.
Trigger notifications when an endpoint changes state.
Chain actions across environments (dev → staging → prod).
Chain actions across environments (dev → staging → prod).
Automation here is intentionally lightweight — just enough logic to remove friction, not replace your system.
*Think of it as the glue between what you see and what you do next.
Step 3: Monitor — Stay aware, not overwhelmed
The final piece is Monitor — real-time awareness without heavy setup. It lets you track the key metrics and signals you actually care about, not an ocean of noise.
Watching API uptime and latency trends.
Watching API uptime and latency trends.
Tracking event rates or job completion times.
Tracking event rates or job completion times.
Setting simple alerts for threshold breaches.
Setting simple alerts for threshold breaches.
You don’t need a full observability stack —a just clear, focused monitoring that keeps your workflow tight.
Why this loop matters aware, not overwhelmed
The “Inspect → Automate → Monitor” loop isn’t a marketing diagram — it’s how modern dev environments actually evolve. You observe a problem, fix it, then make sure it doesn’t come back.
Our goal was to compress that cycle into a single, fluid interface.
So instead of jumping between 5 tools, you can stay in flow.
That’s the core workflow — and the heart of our product.

Start with the CLI or open a sample workspace in the browser — both take less than 2 minutes to set up.

Once you can see your data clearly, the next step is Automate. This module lets you turn any manual debugging step, build routine, or test trigger into a defined workflow.
Run a cleanup task when a new build completes.

Trigger: Defines when the workflow runs — on API call, webhook event, schedule, or user action.

Steps: The logic of your workflow. Chain AI steps, conditions (if / else), loops, and integrations in any order.
Output: What the workflow returns — a structured response, a side effect (email sent, record updated), or both.

Every step name you define becomes available asctx.{step_name}downstream. Keep names short and descriptive — you'll reference them often.

content_slots.source_text: Go beyond prebuilt templates. Custom workflows let you compose AI steps, conditional logic, loops, and external calls into exactly the automation your product needs.
A custom workflow is a directed sequence of steps. Each step takes an input, does something — call an AI model, transform data, hit an API — and passes its output to the next step via context.
Trigger: Defines when the workflow runs — on API call, webhook event, schedule, or user action.

Steps: The logic of your workflow. Chain AI steps, conditions (if / else), loops, and integrations in any order.

Output: What the workflow returns — a structured response, a side effect (email sent, record updated), or both.

Every step name you define becomes available asctx.{step_name}downstream. Keep names short and descriptive — you'll reference them often.
Set a retry policy per step
Any step can fail — network timeouts, model errors, schema mismatches. Define a retry policy at the step level to handle transient failures without rewriting your entire workflow.
Use.onError()to define what happens when a step fails after all retries — log the failure, return a default value, or trigger a different path.

What can I build with this?

You can build AI-powered automation workflows, smart data processing pipelines, content generation tools, and intelligent task routing systems. Aeye is designed for any product that needs to process inputs, apply reasoning, and deliver structured outputs — from internal tools to customer-facing features.
Do I need AI or machine learning experience?

No. Aeye abstracts the underlying AI complexity through clean APIs and workflow primitives. You define what you need — inputs, tasks, and expected outputs — and Aeye handles the rest. Basic programming knowledge is enough to get started.

Install the SDK via npm, pip, or CLI — setup takes under five minutes. Authenticate with your API key, define your workflow, and start sending requests. Aeye returns structured outputs you can plug directly into your existing application logic.
Can it work with my current tools?

Yes. Aeye is built to fit into existing stacks without replacing them. It integrates with common data sources, APIs, and platforms. If your tool can send an HTTP request or run a script, it can connect to Aeye.
Is it suitable for production use?

Yes. Aeye is designed with reliability and consistency in mind — the same input produces the same quality output every time. Teams already use it in live products and automated pipelines, with monitoring and priority support available on higher plans.
